name: Harvest Gold
lede: Harvest Gold is a deep, saturated orange-yellow, the color of ripe grain and, to a generation, of 1970s kitchens.

sections.title: A 1970s kitchen
sections.body:
St Clair places the name in a back-to-nature palette of the 1970s, alongside burnt orange and avocado, when concern for the environment spread into clothing, appliances, baths and cars [1]. The books read give no earlier use of the name. Our library lists the swatch in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system as a deep orange yellow, and the name is also on Wikipedia's lists [2].

The nearest relatives are [[goldenrod]], [[amber]] and [[avocado-green]], the last the era's other signature shade [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In print, the phrase peaks in the 1970s, right on cue [3]. In paintings it is moderately rare: 189 of 23,781 contain it, 0.8 per cent [3]. It is almost always an accent, and it is most over-represented in Indian painting, at 3.6 times the expected rate [3]. George Dawe uses it in 17 of 50 works here, 15 times the baseline of his museums [3]. It often sits with [[caramel]] [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished works [3].
